subject: general
question: A circle with radius r has a tangent line at a point P on the circle. The distance of the tangent from point P to the external point Q is 10 cm. The distance from the center of the circle to point Q is 13 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius to the point of tangency, the tangent segment, and the line to the center form a right-angled triangle.

Radius = √(Distance to Center² − Tangent Length²)

Radius = √(13² − 10²) = √(169 − 100) = √69

**∴ The correct answer is √69 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the tangent PQ = 10 cm

Distance from the center O to external point Q = 13 cm

Radius of the circle = OP = r

**Formula Used:**

Since the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency, ΔOPQ is a right-angled triangle at P.

By Pythagoras Theorem:

OP² + PQ² = OQ²

**Calculations:**

⇒ r² + 10² = 13²

⇒ r² + 100 = 169

⇒ r² = 169 − 100

⇒ r² = 69

⇒ r = √69 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √69 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent Theorem

A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. This angle is always exactly 90°.

Pythagorean Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two legs (h² = p² + b²).

Equal Tangent Lengths

The lengths of the two tangents drawn from a single external point to a circle are perfectly equal to each other.
